## 2026-07-30 (gd) — THE CAGE MUST FIT THE VALUE: 33 of 42 levers had no machine-readable default, and the registry had already drifted from the code

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"if the bounds don't correlate properly then recalibrate individually and have each supporting asset correspond, correlate and optimise."* Suite **367 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green — now six guards, not five.
- **THE FINDING.** A lever is THREE things that must agree: the registry CAGE (`lo`/`hi`), the DECLARED default, and the `os.environ.get` default the consumer ACTUALLY runs. Only the cage was ever machine-readable. **33 of 42 levers carried their default in PROSE inside the `note` field**, and the consumer's real value lived in a different file entirely — so nothing could compare the three, and they had already drifted: `(fz)` moved `scout.ticket_top_n` 6 → 12 in code and its registry note still read *"default 6"* the same afternoon. That is not cosmetic. Every organ that reasons about a lever's HEADROOM — the board's step ladder, the judge's candidate queue, the authority census, a human reading the cage — reasons from the number the registry states. A registry that misdescribes the running value is worse than no registry.
- **RECALIBRATED, INDIVIDUALLY.** All 42 levers now carry a machine-readable `env_default`, each one read from its consumer's own `os.environ.get` call rather than guessed. Measured result: **no default sits outside its cage** and **no cage is degenerate** — so the bounds themselves were sound; what was missing was the ability to KNOW that. Twelve levers are one-sided (default pinned at a bound) and that is reported rather than failed, because it is usually correct: an emission bar sitting at its most restrictive end has all of its room in the growth direction.
- **`scripts/audit_lever_bounds.py` — the new CI guard, and the drift arm is the point.** It enforces (A) every lever has a machine-readable default or a DECLARED exemption, (B) that default lies inside its own cage — a default outside means the very first `get_lever` clamps it, silently changing behaviour nobody asked for, (C) **the registry default MATCHES the consumer's real code default**, parsed by AST from the consuming file, (D) no degenerate cage, and (E) every book lever's `step` actually moves inside the cage and terminates — a step of 0 is an author that can never act. **Mutation-verified end to end**: drifting `SCOUT_TICKET_TOP_N` 12 → 9 in the code while leaving the registry at 12 produces exactly one named failure and nothing else. Negative fixtures cover all five classes. Wired into `changelog-check.yml` and registered in `ENFORCED_AUDITS`.
- **SATURATION IS NOW OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED.** The `(gb)` author judged "is this book at its cap?" from occupancy against the cap the REGISTRY believed it had enacted. Those can legitimately differ — a bot that has not redeployed, a quarantined lever, a TTL that lapsed between the write and the read — and the book's own number is the one that actually gated its trades. The three capacity books now publish `extra.caps`, and the author PREFERS the published cap, falling back to the registry only when absent. Without this an author could judge saturation against a cap it set itself and the bot never adopted, and talk itself into widening forever.
  - **A guard caught me publishing the wrong number.** My first cut published carry's raw `ENTER_APR` — the HL-denominated constant `main()` is explicitly forbidden to touch, because it is the 8x-basis defect. `_selftest_basis` failed the build. The payload now carries `_enter_apr`, the basis-corrected bar the arm actually gates on. The guard was right and the fix is the honest one.
- **WHY THIS IS THE COMPOUNDING PIECE.** `(fz)` gave the books levers, `(ga)` gave them a deploy route, `(gb)` gave them an author and a grader, `(gc)` fixed the auto-revert ratchet that would have made every widening permanent. Each of those is a link. This entry makes the LINKS CHECKABLE: from here a lever cannot be registered with bounds that do not bracket its value, cannot drift from the code its bot runs, and cannot carry an author step that does nothing — and CI says so on every push rather than a reader noticing months later.

## 2026-07-30 (gc) — THE AUTO-REVERT RATCHET: (fz) broke the growth rail's central safety property on all six books, and the new grader was born inert

- **HOW THIS WAS FOUND.** An 8-way parallel organ audit (proprioception, evidence board, immune/regen, fleet-risk, brain, judge/incubator, scout/tuner, dashboard) against the `(fz)`/`(ga)`/`(gb)` tree. It CONFIRMED the authored-by-nobody suspicion `(gb)` had already fixed, and then found **three defects in my own just-shipped work** plus two pre-existing dark consumers. Suite **366 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green.
- **DEFECT 1 — THE ONE-WAY RATCHET, and it is the serious one.** Every `apply_tuning()` `(fz)` shipped did `cur = globals()[attr]` and then `tuning.get_lever(lever, cur)`. `get_lever` returns its **`default`** when a lever is absent, expired or quarantined — so passing the ALREADY-MOVED value meant a widened lever **could never come back**. Auto-revert-on-expiry is not a nicety here, it is the growth rail's stated central safety property (`fleet_tuning` docstring: *"levers EXPIRE back to defaults on their own, so auto-revert is the resting state, not a feature to remember"*), and `(fz)` broke it on all six books simultaneously. It was inert only because `(gb)` had not yet given the lane an author — the two commits together would have armed it. Fixed by snapshotting `_ENV_DEFAULTS` at import in all six bots and handing THAT to `get_lever`. Pinned by a test that moves a lever, expires it, and asserts the revert; the mutation that restores `cur` turns it red.
- **DEFECT 2 — `sniper.apply_tuning()` had NO CALL SITE.** Defined, registered, tested at the unit level, and invoked by nothing: `grep apply_tuning lighter_perp_sniper.py` returned only the `def`. `sniper.surge_mult` could never reach the bot. Now called at the top of the scan loop, and a test asserts EVERY book's `main()` contains a call site.
- **DEFECT 3 — `grade_book` was BORN INERT, which is the exact class it was written to fix.** It read `ep.get("lever")`; a real episode carries **`stance`** (a `{lever: value}` dict) and has no `lever` key at all — as `grade_scout` already knew (`next(iter(ep["stance"]))`). So `bot` was always None and it would have returned `"unmapped-lever"` forever. **My selftest passed because the fixture invented an episode shape the tracker never produces.** Same root cause as the `(gb)` hurting-key bug and the `(fz)` scout-accessor bug: *I keep testing my own invented shape instead of the real contract.* Three times in one session. The fixtures now use the tracker's real shape, and an explicit assertion (`"lever" not in _real_ep`) turns red if it ever regresses.
- **DEFECT 4 — `lever_verdicts` had no branch for book levers.** A perfectly graded book episode produced NO verdict, so no consumer hook — the board's hurting-refusal, the tuner's skip — could ever fire. The grader would have been a dead end even once it graded. Added at the shadow-lane floor (`basis: "book-paired"`), with a test that walks a hurting verdict all the way to `hurting_levers()`, the accessor the board actually reads.
- **PRE-EXISTING, and both silently dark on every HEALTHY cycle:**
  - **The evidence board never FETCHED `fleet-radar`, `parliament` or `parliament-tuning`.** All three are read via `_g()`, but they were absent from `_keys`, and `_g` returns `_b.get(k) or {}` whenever the batch read SUCCEEDS. So the radar's per-book edge classification — the senior corrective on the naive promotion screen, the one that calls the Yield Harvester's +$58 headline an `artifact` — and the entire Parliament section were inert, and only worked when `fetch_states` FAILED and `_g` fell through to per-key loads. A consumer that works only when its own fast path breaks.
  - **`EP_CAP` was a global FIFO.** A burst of ungradeable `recorded` episodes could evict GRADED ones, and graded rows are the only ones `lever_verdicts` can use — including live-lane rows whose verdicts revert a REAL-MONEY lever. Six new book lanes make that burst likely rather than theoretical. Graded rows now hold the budget first; recorded rows fill what is left, chronological order preserved.
- **THE CAPACITY-LEVER METRIC, restated because the audit pushed back on it and the pushback was right to raise it.** `grade_book` asks a different question of capacity levers than of selection levers, and the reason is `grade_live`'s own recorded lesson: `live.clip_scale` is MATHEMATICALLY invariant to per-trade `pnl_pct`, so it fails closed. A capacity lever is NOT invariant — carry prices each trade against a per-position NOTIONAL constant — but demanding a HIGHER mean would reject every capacity widening that ever worked, because a ranked selector reaching deeper takes worse names by construction. So the bar is **"did quality HOLD while throughput rose?"**, with dilution as the detectable failure. That is the honest question for the lever's actual job.
- **STILL OPEN, stated rather than quietly dropped:** four audit readers (immune/regen, brain, judge/incubator, scout/tuner, dashboard) had not returned when this landed. The known-remaining items from the two that did: no book PUBLISHES its effective cap, so the board infers saturation from occupancy alone and cannot distinguish "at the cap" from "at the cap it set itself last cycle"; and the six books are invisible to `fleet_risk`'s EXPOSURE view (deliberately NOT added to the long budget — shadow books must never compete with real strategies for the veto).

## 2026-07-30 (gb) — THE LOOP CLOSES: the books' levers get an AUTHOR and a GRADER, and two dead guards found by asserting against the real payload

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"make every organ integrate with the new information ... grow into what works."* `(fz)` gave six shadow books levers and `(ga)` gave them a deploy route. Both ends of the LEARNING loop were still open — and an open loop is the thing this fleet keeps shipping by accident. Suite **354 passed**, every guard green.
- **THE AUTHOR — the `lighter-books` lane was authored by NOBODY.** `(fz)` bound the lane to the evidence board in `AUTHOR_LANES`, and nothing in `evidence_board.py` wrote it: `board_levers` was populated only from the gapscout ladder (INERT since Gap Scout retired 17-Jul) and `live.clip_scale`. Verified by reading the write site, not assumed. So nine registered, consumed, tested levers **could never move**. That is the exact mirror of the registered-but-not-consumed class, and it would have looked healthy forever.
  - `synthesize_books()` is the missing author, and it is deliberately narrow because a widening author that fires on noise is worse than none: **SATURATED** (holding AT its cap ⇒ turning away already-graded candidates) widens the capacity lever ONE step; **STARVED** (0 open AND no new closes for `BOOK_STARVED_H`) loosens the gate lever ONE step; anything else proposes nothing. A book that is working is left alone.
  - Guards, each selftested: never re-assert a lever graded HURTING; one step per book per cycle; at the registry bound it says nothing; **a MISSING ROW proposes nothing** — absence of evidence must never read as "widen", which is what stops a publish outage ratcheting every book wider on every cycle.
  - The starvation clock needs memory a single snapshot cannot provide, so the board persists `books: {bot: {closed, ts}}` and **restarts the clock only when the close count actually moves**. A missing row KEEPS the prior memory rather than resetting — otherwise a DB blink would restart every window.
- **THE GRADER — book episodes were RECORDED and never judged.** `group_of()` sent them to `other:carry`, and `grade_episode` returns `{"status": "recorded"}` for that, so the tuner's hurting-refusal and the board's helping-walk could never fire for these books. `grade_book()` closes it, and the interesting part is that it asks **two different questions**:
  - **SELECTION levers** (a gate, a ranking, a universe) change WHICH trades are taken, so "did per-trade return improve?" is well-posed.
  - **CAPACITY levers** (more concurrent slots) are where `grade_live`'s hard-won lesson applies but **does not transfer wholesale**. `live.clip_scale` is MATHEMATICALLY invariant to per-trade `pnl_pct` (the clip cancels top and bottom — measured, one distinct value across the whole range) and therefore fails closed. A capacity lever is different: carry prices every trade against a per-position NOTIONAL constant (`funding_carry_bot.py:467`), so the metric does not cancel — but the COMPOSITION changes, because slots 9..12 hold the 9th..12th best candidates. So the honest question is **NOT "did the mean rise"** (it should not; a ranked selector reaching deeper takes worse names — demanding a higher mean would reject every capacity widening that ever worked) but **"did quality HOLD while throughput rose?"** DILUTION is the real failure mode of widening a ranked book, and it is detectable.
- **TWO DEAD GUARDS, both found by checking the payload instead of trusting my own fixture. This is the same mistake `(fz)` recorded for the scout accessor, caught the same way, and it is worth stating that it recurred:**
  1. **The hurting-refusal was reading a key that does not exist.** I wrote `prop_state.get("hurting_levers")`; `fleet_proprioception` publishes `verdicts: {lever: {"verdict": ...}}` — the shape `synthesize_proprioception` in the SAME FILE already reads. The set was always empty, so the single most important guard in the author — never re-widen a lever that measured worse — was silently dead. **My selftest passed because the fixture invented the same wrong key: I tested my mistake, not the contract.** Now asserted against the real shape, plus a symmetry case (a HELPING verdict must NOT block a widening, or the rail freezes permanently).
  2. **`grade_book` would have been structurally incapable of ever grading.** `run_once` fetches `feeds["trades"]` only when an episode's group is in `("live-clip", "live-funding", "live", "xp")` — a `book:*` episode never triggered the fetch, so the grader would have returned "recorded" forever. Wired, tested, and inert. The selftest now asserts the predicate names book groups, so the mutation that removes it turns the test red.
- **ALSO:** book levers gained machine-readable `env_default` + `step` in the registry (the author's ladder arithmetic was otherwise guessing at values documented only in prose), and the ladder rounds — `1.6 - 0.2` is `1.4000000000000001`, which both reads badly in the payload and drifts as steps accumulate, since the no-op check depends on a step landing exactly where the last one left off.
- **VERIFIED AND NOT CHANGED:** the six books are absent from `fleet_risk.FREQTRADE_BOTS`, so `(fz)`'s widening (carry 8→12, Counterweight 10→16 legs, Index 3→10) does **NOT** consume the fleet's 20-long budget and cannot make the risk layer veto the family books. Adding them to that budget would be actively harmful — shadow books would compete with real strategies for the veto. Their invisibility to the EXPOSURE view is a genuine (advisory) gap and is left for the next pass rather than fixed blind.

## 2026-07-30 (ga) — THE BOOKS THAT DO NOT TRADE: the sniper's trigger was unobservable, six services could not auto-deploy, and 7 configured symbols do not exist

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"We cannot have bots not making trades ... the sniper needs its scope fixed ... find and implement whatever auto deploys necessary so that changes can be implemented in real time."* Suite **354 passed**, 25 floors held, every guard green.
- **FIRST, THE ONE THAT INVALIDATED THE LAST COMMIT: six services had NO AUTO-DEPLOY RULE AT ALL.** `lighter_dislocation_bot`, `lighter_funding_spread_bot`, `lighter_index_bot`, `lighter_perp_sniper`, `lighter_trend_bot`, `lighter_family_bot` shipped only when a human ran `railway up`. That applied to `(fz)` **itself** — its levers, widened universes and adaptive gate would have sat in main, green, tested, and reached **no container**. This is the fleet's documented "code was right and was never running" class, and it was sitting under the whole offense pass. All six now have `paths:` entries AND service greps, including the SHARED modules each image carries (`bot_pnl_store`, `paper_broker`, `venues/`, `fleet_tuning`, `fleet_bus`, `funding_basis`) — `(fz)` added `fleet_tuning`/`fleet_bus` to five of these images, so without the shared-module rule the very levers it registered could never have reached them.
  - **HONEST GAP, and it needs one look after the first run:** these services' exact Railway names could NOT be verified from this repo — the only names recorded anywhere are `funding-carry`, `pnl-dashboard`, `market-context` and the two live bots. Hardcoding a guess would red-fail the build (the "Service not found x3" mode the workflow already documents). So the deploy step now **RESOLVES each target against `railway service list`**, reports an unresolvable name as a loud `::warning::` and skips it instead of failing the run, and **prints the real service list** — which is how the next session fixes any name in one pass, with data rather than another guess.
- **THE SNIPER'S SCOPE — the trigger was UNOBSERVABLE, not wrong.** `new_listings` is a market-set **DIFF**: a symbol qualifies for exactly the ONE loop in which it first appears, and only if the process is running with a warm baseline at that exact moment. Miss that loop — a deploy, a restart, a venue hiccup — and the listing is in `baseline` forever. That is why the book has **n=1 close in weeks** with `new_listings: []` on the bus. The thesis (violent repricing in a book with no settled history) was never the problem.
  - **`young_candidates()` — the third source, and the one that actually reaches.** A book with `<= SNIPER_YOUNG_MAX_BARS` (21) daily candles is in the same debut regime and stays observable for **weeks**. Measured on the venue for calibration: the majors carry **~402 daily bars**, so a handful of bars is unambiguous. Ordered YOUNGEST first (closest to the debut, where the move is), filtered on real turnover (`YOUNG_MIN_VOL_M` — a debut with no volume is a ghost print, and this bot's own history is full of one-sided debut books), deduped against the same ledger the surge source uses, bounded per loop.
  - The candle probe is **GOVERNED** (`YOUNG_PROBE_BUDGET=4`/loop, the venue REST budget is shared) and **MONOTONE**: a book measured past the young bar enters `not_young` **permanently**, because books only ever age. So the probe cost decays to zero once the venue has been walked once, and the cache is safe to persist.
- **SCOPE HYGIENE — 7 configured symbols DO NOT EXIST on Lighter.** Measured against the live venue with `ctx.supports()`: **family core 2/15 dead (ATOM, ALGO)**, family WIDE 4/29 (ATOM, ETC, ALGO, INJ), **Counterweight 5/30 dead (INJ, RUNE, STX, GALA, W)**. Typed when the venue carried a different set, never re-checked. Dead names cost a backfill call each, make `len(COINS)` a lie in every log line, and on a book that needs `2*K` rankable coins to rebalance at all they can be the difference between rebalancing and skipping. `prune_dead()` now drops them at boot and NAMES them in the log. **Fail-safe direction matters here and is tested: a `supports()` that RAISES KEEPS the coin** — an unreachable venue must never silently empty a book's universe, which would be this same commit causing the exact disease it is treating.
- **A HYPOTHESIS I CHECKED AND WAS WRONG ABOUT, recorded because the check is the point.** I expected the near-zero books (mum 0 closes, crypto-swing-daily 1, avo-maria 4) to be starved by insufficient candle history — SwingDip needs `min_bars=230` and `SPAN_BARS['1d']` is 240, a 10-bar margin. Measured instead: **the majors carry 402 daily bars**, so history is not the binding constraint for the family's core universe. The `min_bars` margin is still thin enough to be worth knowing, and the measurement is what produced the sniper's 402-bar calibration — but the family books' low turnover is NOT a data-availability bug and must not be "fixed" as one.
- **A REAL BUG THE NEW TESTS CAUGHT BEFORE MERGE:** `young_candidates` coerced symbols with a bare `str(sym)`, so a `None` key became the string `"NONE"` and would have entered the snipe pass as a tradable-looking candidate. Fixed at the function (`isinstance(sym, str)`), not at the test.
- **TESTS: 40 -> 49** in `tests/autonomy/test_book_levers.py` — the young-book cohort (ordering, turnover floor, dedup, bounds, junk), the probe cache's governed-and-monotone construction, and `prune_dead`'s never-empty-a-book-on-a-venue-error contract.

## 2026-07-30 (fz) — THE OFFENSE PASS: six books get levers, five get the venue's real universe, and the fleet's tightest supply cap doubles

- **THE ASK** (operator): *"optimise all bots, enhance their integrations ... every bot needs every tool at its disposal and every bot needs the ability to grow."* This is `(fy)`'s ranked list, implemented. Suite **345 passed** (was 305), **25 coverage floors** held (was 19), every guard green.
- **THE STRUCTURAL FINDING BEHIND ALL OF IT: six books had ZERO registered levers.** 🌾 Yield Harvester, ⚖️ Counterweight, 🧲 Snap Back, 📊 Index Rider, 🌊 Tide Rider, 🎯 Perp Sniper. The growth rail could not move a single knob on any of them — including **`carry.enter_apr`, the best-performing gate in the fleet** (+$56.20 realised, n=80, t=2.42, both halves positive). "The ability to grow" is not a metaphor: it is registry membership PLUS a consumer that actually reads it, and they had neither. New lane **`lighter-books`** (author: evidence board only — it gains NO new reach into real money; the judge remains the sole writer of `live.funding.*`), nine levers, each consumed by an `apply_tuning()` called every loop.
- **THE SUPPLY CAP — `SCOUT_TICKET_TOP_N` 6 → 12.** `strategy_tickets` truncates EVERY lens to this number, and on the live bus `dip` and `divergence` both returned **exactly 6** while breakout/momentum returned 5 — a lens returning exactly its cap is a lens whose cap binds. The lens behind it is the fleet's only measured alpha (shadow short-divergence **+3.035%/trade vs its own regime, t=+4.04**), and it was being handed a 6-wide candidate list from which to fill 4 slots. Every "closed question" on the Taker (`TT_MAX_OPEN`, `TT_DIV_GAP`, lens on/off, clip size, symbol eligibility) was about **ALLOCATING** that fixed supply; **none of them was about ENLARGING it.** Widening moves no entry bar — the taker's own gates still judge every ticket.
- **THE INTEGRATION — `fleet_bus.scout_universe()` / `.scout_funding()` / `.venue_stress_bps()`.** Five books carried hand-typed watchlists written when Lighter was much smaller: Counterweight ranked **30 of 202 books** (15%), Snap Back 16 (8%), Tide Rider 6, Index Rider 3. A ranked selector cannot pick a winner it never sees, and unlike loosening a gate, enlarging the candidate set does not weaken the selection rule at all. The scout already scans every book each cycle, so this is a read of work already done.
  - **A REAL BUG CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, recorded because the class matters:** the first cut of this accessor read `marks[sym]["vol_m"]` and `stress["med_bps"]`. The scout's actual payload is `marks = {sym: PRICE}` (a float) and `stress = {..., "med": ...}` — so the accessor would have returned an empty universe and a permanent `None` stress **against every real payload**, while its own selftest passed on a fixture I had invented. Caught by diffing the fixture against the LIVE `/bus.json`. The selftest now asserts against the scout's real key names, and the scout publishes an explicit public **`vols`** map (the data existed only in `_marks`, documented as a private diff base no consumer should bind to). The accessor still falls back to `_marks` so a consumer shipped ahead of the scout's next deploy is not dark.
  - **CONTRACT, and it is the important part:** any doubt returns `[]`/`{}`/`None`, and **every caller must read empty as "keep my configured list", never as "trade nothing"**. The widening is an ENHANCEMENT, never a DEPENDENCY — no organ outage may shrink a book's universe. Tested per consumer against a dark bus, a stale bus, a RAISING bus and a born-dark import.
- **PER BOOK, with the measurement that motivated each:**
  - 🌾 **Carry `MAX_POSITIONS` 8 → 12** — measured at **7 open of 8**: the fleet's biggest earner was one slot from full and turning away carries it had already graded. Its 38.8% win rate is not a defect; carry's return lives in the tail, which is exactly why refusing graded candidates is expensive.
  - ⚖️ **Counterweight `K` 5 → 8, universe 30 → up to 60** — measured **AT its structural cap**: 10 open = exactly K=5 × 2 legs. It still takes exactly top-K/bottom-K, now from a real cross-section.
  - 🧲 **Snap Back: the fixed 150bps gate becomes a PERCENTILE of the live residual** (`adaptive_enter_bps`, default p98). 150bps was ~**40× its own median residual** (3.8bps) and predates the 17-Jul switch off Hyperliquid's mid — the reference changed and the constant never did. **FLOORED at `EXIT_BPS × 1.5` and CAPPED at the operator constant**: entering nearer the exit bar than that books a capture smaller than the round trip that earns it. **Say the honest thing: on today's tape the floor will usually bind, so the practical effect is 150 → ~60bps, not "the gate follows the median down".** The percentile matters on genuinely dislocated days, which are the days this book exists for. Universe 16 → 40 (dislocations are commoner in thin books — exactly where the hand list had no coverage).
  - 📊 **Index Rider: universe 3 → 10, clip $250 → $100.** It carried the **LARGEST CLIP IN THE FLEET** — 5× the family's $50, 10× the Farmer's $25 — on a book with **ZERO closed trades**: maximum size on minimum evidence, the exact inversion of how everything else here is sized. The ten non-crypto books are the fleet's **only source of a regime that is not falling-BTC** (SPY +8.1%, QQQ +12.2%, WTI +23.0% over the same window) — the on-venue answer to item 18. Widened sleeves reuse the ALREADY-VALIDATED rules (200-day band for index-like, 20/50 cross for single names and commodities), so the change is one variable, not two.

Its event (a brand-new listing) is too rare to grade: **n=1 close in weeks**, and `new_listings` is routinely empty. A strategy that cannot accumulate a sample cannot be validated, improved, or retired on evidence. **The subtlety, which is why this needed its own ledger:** every surging book is ALREADY in `baseline` (seeded with all active markets), so baseline cannot dedup this source the way it dedups listings — without the persisted `surge_done` set a surging book would re-enter `pending` every loop forever. (`enter_apr`'s ceiling was already widened to 0.12 by `(ex,ey)` — that item of `(fy)`'s list was closed before this pass began.)

- **TESTS — `tests/autonomy/test_book_levers.py`, 40 tests**, built around the two failure classes that matter: a lever REGISTERED BUT NOT CONSUMED (enacted on the bus, changes no trade — the 17-Jul `FLEET_RISK_MODE` shape), and a widening that becomes a DEPENDENCY (a book that shrinks because an organ is down). Plus the adaptive gate's floor/cap/thin-sample/side-blindness, and every optimised default pinned so a silent revert is visible.

- **THE THIRD CORRECTION, same species as the first two.** `(fs)` fixed pooling across the 24-Jul bull flip. `(fv)` then claimed pooled **n=21 / t=+2.86** as "the edge is real". That pools **11 live trades run on ONE exit bracket with 10 shadow trades run on FOUR** — the scout tuner was moving the shadow's bars mid-window. **Two arms, five policies, one t-statistic.** Verified straight from the ledger's own `extra.bars`, no replay involved:

  | arm | n | distinct bar-sets in the era |
  |---|---|---|
  | **LIVE** | 11 | **1** — `sl -0.03 / tp 0.04 / hold 48h`, all 11 |
  | **SHADOW** | 10 | **4** — `-0.04/0.05/24h` x5, `-0.04/0.06/72h` x2, `-0.04/0.03/24h` x2, `-0.04/0.06/24h` x1 |

- **GRADED ON THE ONE CLEAN SINGLE-POLICY SAMPLE THAT EXISTS** — the live arm's own 11 closes: **+0.883%/trade, t=+0.73** (ddof=1), 95% CI **[-1.81%, +3.57%] straddling zero**, and `golive_readiness.py` fails it on 4 of 6 bars (window 4.2d, n=11, t<2.0, halves -0.96/+1.98; it passes mean>0 and maxDD 2.20%). Leave-one-symbol-out keeps the mean positive in all 7 folds but **never reaches significance** (max t=+1.07) — sign-stable, magnitude-unstable, never significant. **The honest verdict is "positive and insignificant", not "the edge is real".**
- **AND THE 4x CAPTURE GAP IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY, VIEWED FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** 84% of it is those same stamped bar differences — 5 paired tickets (same symbol, entries <=2 min apart) sum to **+10.939pp with ZERO residual** for fills, timing, funding or ticket quality. So "close the gap" means **adopting the shadow's bars — letting a shadow-replay-gated author steer real money**, which is exactly what `apply_tuning()`'s live-venue early return exists to forbid. The gap is not a defect to fix; it is the live arm being structurally immune to the growth rail. `(fw)`'s decomposition stands and this sharpens it.
- **WHAT SHIPS — the missing field, not a config change.** `_close_extra()` now stamps `extra.policy = {bull, lenses, venue, max_open}` on every close row. The bars stamp records the EXIT bracket and is **byte-identical across the bull flip**, so the ledger's only trace of a policy change was the `reason` tag flipping long->short — a downstream symptom a grader must already know to look for. That single missing field produced **two opposite errors**: `(fp)`/`(fr)`'s *"n=25, t=-0.26, no edge"* and `(fv)`'s over-corrected *"pooled t=+2.86, the edge is real"*. With it, any grader — `golive_readiness`, `bot_learn`, the experiment judge, `fleet_proprioception`, or a human — can split eras **mechanically**. Observable-only; `setdefault` means it can never clobber `bars`/`bars_basis` or an evidence key.
- **THE DELIBERATE NON-ACTION: the live config is FROZEN for the rest of the window, and that is an active decision.** The live arm has exactly ONE clean single-policy era (all 11 closes share an identical bars stamp; the row publishes `tuned=[]`, structurally guaranteed by the live-venue early return). **Any env change resets that era clock to day 0.** And the binding go-live constraint is CALENDAR, not trade count: at the measured 2.275 closes/day the `n>=30` bar is met around **day 13** while the `>=30-day` bar is met on **day 30** — so changing config to buy more closes buys nothing and costs the whole window. Both route proposals from the campaign (`TT_MAX_OPEN`->2 with a $20 clip; raising `TT_CLIP_MIN` with the cap) are therefore **rejected**, and both measured NEGATIVE on the real live fills anyway.
- **Also measured, and it retires the capital question at the mechanical level:** raising `LIGHTER_TICKET_TAKER_MAX_NOTIONAL` alone is **exactly $0** — zero cap-skips in the whole tape, and the ladder from $40 to no-cap is flat. The rail never binds (mean concurrency 2.31 of 4 slots), so lifting it changes nothing. Whether the edge deserves more money is a separate question, and it cannot be argued honestly for another ~25 days.

## 2026-07-29 (fy) — FLEET OFFENSE ANALYSIS: the entry bar of the live Farmer sits at the MEDIAN of the venue, and the three best books are all at a structural cap

- **THE ASK** (operator): what metrics/gates/scanners/bounds/scope each bot carries, and how each can **win more** — explicitly not how to lose less. `FLEET_OFFENSE_ANALYSIS_2026-07-29.md`. Gate surfaces read at `3761620`; fleet P&L and signal bus pulled LIVE from `/pnl.json` + `/bus.json`; funding distribution computed over all 202 books the scout reports. No code changed.
- **THE SCOREBOARD SAYS ONE THING: every profitable book in this fleet is a FUNDING book.** Carry +$56.20, Farmer shadow +$14.21, Taker shadow +$7.80 (its live edge is SHORT-divergence, a funding signal), live Farmer +$6.85, Counterweight +$6.83. Every DIRECTIONAL book — four family books, three spot ports, Tide Rider, Index Rider, five of six PMs — is flat or negative. On a 438d tape that is one falling-BTC regime this is exactly what item 18 predicts, and it means the offense budget belongs in the funding complex where the regime caveat bites least. Second fact: **the two biggest earners win 38.8% and 37.8% of their trades** — `(fk)` established for the GATE that win rate is orthogonal to expectancy; several bot gates still implicitly optimise hit-rate, which on this evidence is the wrong objective.
- **THE REFRAME — every book is in exactly one of three states, and the fix differs in each.** (A) CAPACITY/SLOT-BOUND: carry **7 open of MAX_POSITIONS=8**, Counterweight **10 open = exactly K=5 x 2 legs**, live Taker at `MAX_OPEN=4` + the $40 rail (`TT_MAX_OPEN` is INERT because the rail binds first). (B) SIGNAL-BOUND: Farmer **0 open of 6 on BOTH arms**, Snap Back's gate at 150bps vs a measured 3.8bps median residual, sniper with `new_listings: 0`. (C) SAMPLE-STARVED: **8 of 23 books have fewer than 13 closes** (mum 0, Tide Rider 0, Index Rider 0, swing-daily 1, sniper 1, avo-maria 4, dad 9, breakout-4h 12) — at the go-live bar of >=30 closes over >=30 days most are YEARS from decidable. Winning more starts with making those books decidable or retiring them.
- **FINDING — `FUNDING_ENTER_APR=0.05` ADMITS 57% OF THE VENUE. It is not a selection gate, it is a coin flip.** Measured over all 202 books: p25 3.5% / **median 10.5% / p75 10.5%** / p90 28.9% / max 196.2%. The distribution has a hard spike AT the venue's 10.5% baseline, so the information is in the tail ABOVE the spike and the Farmer's bar sits BELOW it. Worse, `live.funding.enter_apr`'s lever ceiling is **0.075 — below the venue's own mode** — so the growth rail CANNOT express "only take above-median funding" (this is the review's queued item A1; the distribution above is the argument for it).
  - **The fleet already ran the natural experiment.** 🌾 Carry is the same funding signal on the same venue with a **4x tighter bar** (20% TRUE = top 14% of books) and a **5x looser liquidity floor** ($2M vs $10M) — and it is the fleet's biggest earner on a near-identical close count (80 vs 84). Its `artifact` classification does not undercut this, it IS the point: **carry's return lives in the tail, and a tail-seeking bar is what exposes a book to it.** A median-seeking bar is structurally incapable of that return shape.
- **FINDING — the liquidity floors cut the fleet off from its own tail.** Of the venue's 8 most extreme funding books RIGHT NOW, `FUNDING_MIN_VOL=$10M` excludes **five, including the two most extreme** (H100 −99.0% at $0.14M, XLM −89.4% at $0.26M, SKR −78.8% at $0.25M, XPD +47.3% at $0.11M, TRUMP −41.2% at $0.22M). Same shape on the Taker's alpha lens: **every one of its 6 divergence tickets is a sub-$1M book** ($0.18–0.63M). The slip/spread gates (`SCAN_MAX_SLIP_BPS 25`, `MAX_SPREAD_BPS 20`) already measure the actual clip cost that `MIN_VOL` is only a crude proxy for.
- **THIS EXPLAINS THE TAKER'S CLIP RESULT, AND FLIPS ITS PRESCRIPTION.** $13.33 → +$2.26, $20 → −$1.57, $40 → −$2.22 is not evidence against the edge — it is a **capacity curve**; you cannot push $40 through a $0.3M book. The campaign handoff calls the book "capital-bound"; the data says **capacity-bound**, and those have OPPOSITE prescriptions. A per-trade edge that decays with size is harvested by **breadth (more trades, more books, more slots at small clip)**, never by depth. Do not size up the live Taker.
- **FINDING — the scout truncates the fleet's best signal to SIX tickets.** `lighter_market_scout.py:304` hard-caps every lens at `TICKET_TOP_N=6`; on the live bus `dip` and `divergence` both return **exactly 6** (breakout/momentum return 5) — a lens returning exactly its cap is a lens whose cap binds. So the strategy measured at **+3.035%/trade vs regime, t=+4.04** is fed a 6-wide list and then picks 4. Every "closed question" on the Taker (`TT_MAX_OPEN`, `TT_DIV_GAP`, lens on/off, clip size, symbol eligibility) was about ALLOCATING a fixed 6-wide supply; **none of them was about enlarging it.** `scout.ticket_top_n` is already a registered replay-gated lever — this is the highest-leverage single knob in the fleet.
- **FINDING — the universes are hand-typed watchlists the venue outgrew.** Counterweight ranks 30 of 202 books (15%), Snap Back 16 (8%), family 15–29, Tide Rider 6, Index Rider 3. Only the two funding books that scan venue-wide discover anything. Enlarging a candidate set does not weaken the selection rule at all — Counterweight still takes its top-5/bottom-5, just from a real cross-section.
- **RANKED ACTIONS** (full table in the doc, each naming the shadow book it is tested on first): 1) `scout.ticket_top_n` 6→10–12; 2) carry `MAX_POSITIONS` 8→12; 3) Counterweight `K` 5→8 + universe 30→~98; 4) raise the `enter_apr` lever CEILING to 0.12+ and walk the shadow arm up through the existing judge; 5) Farmer `MIN_VOL` $10M→~$2M on the shadow arm; 6) register carry's `ENTER_APR` as a lever (**the best-performing gate in the fleet is currently untunable**); 7) re-base Snap Back's `ENTER_BPS` on a measured residual percentile; 8) build the explore prefilter (`SCAN_EXPLORE_K=0`, explore has structurally never fired); 9) give one PM a funding lens; 10) decide the Class-C books.
- **ALSO RECORDED — Index Rider carries the LARGEST CLIP IN THE FLEET ($250, 5x the family's $50, 10x the Farmer's $25) on a book with ZERO closed trades** — maximum size on minimum evidence, the exact inversion of how everything else is sized. And `TT_STRESS_VETO_BPS` has never fired (0/2397 snapshots): a gate that has never fired has never been tested either.
- **WHAT NOT TO DO, stated so the offense framing cannot be read as a licence:** do not size up the live Taker; do not re-open `TT_DIV_GAP` or the exit ladder (swept to their degenerate limits, no interior optimum — re-opening them is how the `(fm)`/`(fo)` artifact loop happened); do not widen directional crypto books on "both halves positive" (item 18 — one regime, so a directional short passes BY CONSTRUCTION); do not treat win rate as the objective; and do not relax restrict-only doctrine to ship any of it — every item is expressible as a bounded TTL'd replay-gated lever or a shadow-arm experiment under the existing judge.

## 2026-07-29 (fw) — THE CAPTURE GAP IS EXPLAINED AND ~0% RECOVERABLE: it is slot luck and a censoring artifact, not skill the live arm is missing

- **THE QUESTION `(fs)` OPENED.** Same era, same ticket stream, live **+0.883%/trade** vs shadow **+3.484%**. That 2.601pp gap looked like the biggest prize on the book. It is not: **~13% is recoverable at the absolute most, and realistically ~0%.**
- **THE DECOMPOSITION**, in per-trade percentage points of the 2.601pp gap:

  | cause | share | $ over the 5.2d window | recoverable? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **slot-saturation LUCK** — the shadow skipped tickets because it was FULL, not because it chose better | **55.8%** (+1.451pp) | $1.74 | **$0 — not a defect** |
  | **CENSORING artifact** — the shadow's wider bars keep losing positions OUT of its closed-trade ledger | ~13% | ~$1.25 | **not money** (-0.89pp once open positions are marked to market) |
  | stop width (live -0.03 vs shadow -0.04) | 30.6% (+0.797pp) | $0.96 | only by widening a real-money stop — **already refuted `(fo)`** |
  | take-profit height | (+0.198pp) | $0.24 | **negative standalone** — raising tp without the stop makes live worse |
  | FILLS / SLIPPAGE | — | **-$0.16** | **REFUTED, and backwards: live fills CHEAPER** |
  | ENTRY TIMING | — | +$0.19 (one SKHY case) | **REFUTED** — live enters later but at a BETTER price |
  | FUNDING | — | +$0.03 | live IS receiving it, it IS in the ledger, ~zero both arms |
  | **CLIP SIZE / the $40 cap** | — | **~$11.85 of the $15.01 total** | **STRUCTURAL — a $66 book cannot be a $1k book** |

- **THE THREE HYPOTHESES I WAS MOST CONFIDENT IN ARE ALL DEAD.** I proposed fills, entry timing and funding capture as the likely causes. Fills run the *other way* (live is cheaper by $0.16), live's entry timing gets a *better* average price, and funding is being collected and recorded and is ~zero for both arms. Recording that plainly because "the live arm must be getting worse fills" is exactly the kind of plausible story that survives on plausibility alone.
- **THE CENSORING FINDING IS THE SUBTLE ONE and it generalises beyond this book.** A wider bracket does not only change outcomes — it changes WHICH positions have closed yet. The shadow's losers were still open and therefore absent from its closed-trade mean; marking them to market costs it **-0.89pp**. **Any live-vs-shadow comparison between arms running different bars is biased in favour of the wider-barred arm** until open positions are included. That is a standing methodology hazard for the experiment judge's paired bar, not a one-off.
- **WHAT IT MEANS.** The live arm is NOT leaving skill on the table — it drew worse symbols in a 10-trade sample and its twin's ledger flatters itself by deferring losses. Combined with `(fu)` (configuration closed, ~455 configs) and `(fv)` (inversion is drift, but short-divergence has real alpha), **every route to more realised profit that does not require capital or time is now measured and closed.**
- **SIDE FINDING, unresolved and worth a look:** a shadow stop fired on a mark the fill disagreed with (~$0.42 on that trade; excluding it moves the shadow mean 3.484 -> 3.635%). Not gap-driving, but it means a stop can fire on a price the book never traded. Logged in the handoff.
- Read-only research. No lever, no bar, no book, no real money.

## 2026-07-29 (fv) — "IF IT LOSES, IT CAN WIN" — TESTED, and it is the falling market. But the same test found the Taker's edge is REAL ALPHA, not drift

- **THE OPERATOR'S IDEA, taken seriously and measured.** *"Think outside the box — if it loses, it can win."* The arithmetic is sound: a loser worse than twice the round-trip fee inverts to a winner, because `inverted = -r_net - 2f`. Swept across every lens/side the Taker has ever traded, exactly one candidate cleared the bar: **inverting `long-dip` gives +1.082%/trade at t=+2.48 on n=13** (not the naive +1.162% — flipping pays the fee twice).
- **AND IT IS THE REGIME, not an edge.** Lighter's tape is one falling-BTC market, so a LONG-biased lens loses BY CONSTRUCTION and inverting it just shorts a falling market — CLAUDE.md item 18, which the repo has asserted since 21-Jul but never measured. The test: subtract the MEDIAN return of taking the same direction in every liquid Lighter book over the SAME window.

  | candidate | raw | vs short-everything | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | inverted `long-dip` | +1.082% (t=**+2.48**) | **+0.098% (t=+0.14)** | **DRIFT** |

  The benchmark column shows why: over those same windows, shorting anything earned +1.75%, +2.33%, +2.89%, +3.03%. **Nearly all of the "edge" was the market falling.** A serious-looking candidate, killed by the right test.
- **THE SAME TEST VINDICATES THE LIVE POLICY, and this is the strongest result of the day.** Subtracting the drift makes short-divergence STRONGER, which is the signature of genuine cross-sectional selection rather than beta:

  | book / lens (current era) | n | raw | vs-market | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | shadow `short-divergence` | 10 | +3.484% (t=+4.86) | **+3.035% (t=+4.04)** | **ALPHA** |
  | live `short-divergence` | 11 | +0.883% (t=+0.73) | +1.223% (t=+1.11) | positive, under-powered |
  | shadow `long-breakoutup` | 8 | -1.973% | -0.828% (t=-0.61) | no alpha |

  Across ALL history the same lens is `n=95, vs-market +0.347%, t=+1.23` — so **the alpha is specific to the post-bull-flip era**, consistent with `(fs)`'s 57-trade losing prior and with the gate being the mechanism.
- **A USEFUL NEGATIVE that changes how `dip` should be read**: `long-dip`'s raw `t=-2.66` looked like a significantly BAD lens. Against the benchmark it is **+0.173%, t=+0.36** — dip has no negative alpha either. It simply went long in a falling market. Nothing about dip is anti-predictive; it is direction-exposed. That is a materially different verdict from "dip loses" and it should be quoted that way.
- **SHIPPED: `scripts/study_alpha_vs_regime.py`** — the instrument item 18 has needed since 21-Jul. Direction-matched benchmark (benchmarking a short against a long market would credit the strategy with the whole drift), MEDIAN not mean (a handful of 1000-scaled meme books would otherwise set the bar alone), refuses to invent a market below 20 quoted books, sample-stdev t per `(fs)`. Selftest discriminates **all four** cases — drift with a huge raw t, genuine skill, NEGATIVE alpha, and the thin-cross-section refusal — because a detector that can only say "no alpha" is not a detector. Verified to reproduce both live findings end-to-end.
- **WHAT THIS MEANS FOR "MAKE IT WIN".** The strategy is not the problem: it has measurable alpha over its own regime. Configuration is closed (`(fu)`: ~455 configs, zero survivors). Inversion is closed (this entry). **What is left is sample and size** — the live arm is n=11 with vs-market t=+1.11, directionally consistent with the shadow's t=+4.04 but not yet significant on its own. More closes fix the first; only capital fixes the second, and the operator's own gate wants 30 days before that conversation.
- Read-only research + one new script. No lever, no bar, no book, no real money.

## 2026-07-29 (fu) — THE CONFIG SPACE IS CLOSED: ~455 configurations, four families, ZERO survivors — and two of the biggest knobs are provably unreachable

- **THE VERDICT: NO SUPPORTED CHANGE.** A 12-agent search swept ~455 distinct live-arm configurations against a bar written down BEFORE it ran (interior optimum; both halves at 72/120/168/200h; leave-one-symbol-out; not-within-noise; tail check; reachability). Nothing survived. Every measured config lands within **+/-$3.3 of zero on $10 clips — a third of ONE clip — with |t| never exceeding 1.31.** Both family argmaxes sit BELOW the `t>=2.0` the fleet's own gate demands of a PAPER book; shipping either would steer real money on evidence the fleet refuses to promote a shadow book on.
- **TWO KNOBS ARE PROVABLY UNREACHABLE, which closes them permanently rather than merely failing them today:**
  - **The stress veto has NEVER FIRED.** `stress.med` across all 2397 snapshots: min 3.80, max 9.20, p99 8.70, against a deployed **15bps** bar. Snapshots at or above it: **ZERO**. Setting `TT_STRESS_VETO_BPS=1e9` (veto removed entirely) returns a byte-identical book — same net, same n, same 38 trades. The deployed value **already sits on the degenerate limit of its own ladder**, so loosening it is not a small effect, it is provably nothing.
  - **`TT_MAX_OPEN` is pinned by the RAIL, not by itself.** `venues/safety.py` `notional_ok()` admits an entry only while `open_notional + clip <= max_notional`; at `cap_usd=40` and $10 clips that is exactly **4** concurrent positions — the same point `TT_MAX_OPEN=4` binds. Every value from 5 upward replays byte-identically on the real-money arm. (With the rail NOT modelled the ladder does move — 5: +1.72, 6: +1.02, unlimited: +0.68 — which proves the flatness is the operator's cap, not the tape.)
- **AND THE LIVE ARM HAS NO AUTONOMOUS TUNING PATH AT ALL**, by deliberate design: `lighter_ticket_taker.apply_tuning()` returns `{}` outright when `TT_VENUE == "lighter_live"` (:310, and the docstring explains why — only `live.*` levers may steer real money, and `taker.*` belongs to the shadow lane's replay-gated author). So every `taker.*` bar on the live arm is **operator-env-only**. Good governance, and worth stating plainly: no organ can improve this book, only a human.
- **HOW EACH FAMILY DIED** — the mechanisms are worth more than the numbers:
  - **stress-veto** (85 configs): loosening is unreachable (above). TIGHTENING is reachable below 9.2bps and does show an interior peak (+$3.03 at 7.6bps), so it survives the artifact test — then dies on noise and on MECHANISM. The peak **moves under grid refinement** (7.9bps coarse, 7.6bps fine) and diffing 7.5 vs 7.6 leaves n unchanged at 34 with 29 of 34 trades shared: the veto is not filtering bad trades, it is **shifting which snapshot a position opens on**. A BOT short opens 23-Jul 23:07 at bar 7.5 and loses -3.32%; at bar 7.6 the SAME signal opens 23:02 — five minutes earlier — and wins +4.12%. A **7.4pp single-trade swing from a 0.1bps move** is most of the "improvement".
  - **cooldown-concurrency** (54): `TT_SL_COOLDOWN_H` laddered to both degenerate ends, and the argmax IS the no-filter endpoint at all four windows — rank 1 of 14, every time. Same shape that killed the exit bracket. Cleanest result: the deployed 2h cooldown cuts no tail (worst -5.12% unchanged from 0h to 6h) while **every** cooldown >=8h has a strictly WORSE worst trade (-6.15%).
  - **symbol-eligibility** (52): family-wide noise kill (best is +$0.23 over deployed = 2.3% of one clip; per-symbol P&L spans only [-$0.98, +$0.58], so there is no chronic loser to cut). Structural finding worth keeping: **under a BINDING max_open, excluding a symbol is SUBSTITUTION, not subtraction — and the substitute is reliably worse.** Excluding the 1000-scaled books removed 4 fills and added 4 (n unchanged) while pushing the worst trade -5.12% -> -6.15%. Same slot-competition mechanism that killed lens-mix `(fl)`, one level down.
  - **entry-timing** (~264): "enter earlier" **does not exist as a direction** — 34 of 38 live entries already occur at episode age 0, 37 of 38 at age <=1. The one candidate that passed the middle criteria (min episode age k=12, +$1.88) is +3.31 sd above its own 60-rung ladder mean where E[max] of 60 draws is ~+2.3 sd, and its neighbours are k=10 +0.19 / k=14 -0.10 — a single-point spike whose entry-age histogram `{12: 12, 41: 1}` shows it is not selecting mature episodes, it is pinning entry to a fixed 60-minute delay.
- **`TT_SPREAD_GATE_BPS` cannot be evaluated at all**: divergence tickets carry exactly `{sym, side, vol_m, gap_pct, prem_bps, xvenue_apr, lighter_apr, regime}` across all 10,597 of them. No spread, no bid, no ask. Not refuted — **unmeasurable on this instrument**.
- **The TRADFI leak is confirmed a third time and its price restated**: 5 of 38 live fills are SK Hynix leaking through a gate that names it (`SKHYNIX` vs the venue's `SKHY`/`SKHYNIXUSD`), plus TENCENT and CXMT. Fixing it MEASURES WORSE (+$1.45 -> +$1.15, second half negative at all four windows). Per `(fr)`: if the operator wants the gate to mean what it says, ship it as a **correctness** change and say plainly that it costs money on this tape. Do not dress it as an edge.
- **WHAT THIS LEAVES.** Configuration is not the binding constraint and is now closed as a line of enquiry. The binding constraints are **supply** (~26% duty cycle), **sample** (n=38 replayed / n=11 live in the current era), and **capital** ($66.45 behind a $40 rail at ~$10 a clip). The first two are answered by TIME; the third is the operator's. No further config sweep should be run on this book without new tape or a new instrument — that is the point of recording all four death mechanisms here.

## 2026-07-29 (ft) — THE STOP QUESTION, RE-OPENED BY REAL MONEY: the tail (fo) called missing is real, AND a -4% stop would have earned +11.41pp on the live arm's own five stop-outs

- **WHY THIS EXISTS.** `(fs)` corrected the live Taker's edge from "negative" to real. That exposed a live-vs-shadow puzzle: in the SAME era on the SAME ticket stream the live arm earned **+0.883%/trade** and its twin **+3.484%/trade**. The mechanical difference in the ledger is stark — **the live arm stopped out 5 times in 11 trades; the shadow stopped out ONCE in 10** — and during that era the shadow was running the tuner's `sl=-0.04` while live ran `-0.03`.
- **THE COUNTERFACTUAL, priced exactly on the five REAL positions** (short returns reconstructed from the scout tape's own marks, 48h max hold):

  | symbol | realised @ -3% | would be @ -4% | delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | WLD | -3.34% | **+4.00%** (tp) | **+7.34pp** |
  | DATA | -3.44% | **+2.96%** (hold 48h) | **+6.40pp** |
  | 1000PEPE | -3.55% | -4.00% | -0.45pp |
  | DRAM | -2.98% | -4.00% | -1.02pp |
  | SKHY | -3.13% | -4.00% | -0.87pp |
  | | | **NET** | **+11.41pp** (= +$1.14 at the $10 clip) |

  Two saves, three small costs. On the live arm's 11 era trades that is roughly +0.883% -> **+1.9%/trade**.
- **[CORRECTED, same day, before merge — an independent regrade tested this against reality and it is weaker than the table implies.]** The counterfactual is a MODEL result, not an observed one. **WLD is the falsifiable row and the real world disagreed with it**: the SHADOW arm actually ran `sl=-0.04` on WLD two minutes later and realised **-0.132%**, not the +4.00% my table projects. The reconciliation is that the shadow's `max_hold` was **24h** in that window while my simulation used live's own **48h** — the +4% move happened between 24h and 48h. So the row is internally sound as a SINGLE-variable change at live's hold, and simultaneously the nearest real instance of a -4% stop on that symbol lost money. **Both are true; neither is decisive at n=5.**
- **AND THE SAME DATA REFUTES THE NAIVE READ. THE TAIL IS REAL.** `(fo)` reverted the live stop partly because, on the replay, the no-stop configuration's worst trade (-3.35%) was SMALLER than the deployed stop's own worst — "this window contains no tail". **These real positions travelled to -5.85% (DRAM) and -6.01% (SKHY).** The tail was never missing; it was absent from the REPLAY'S ENTRY SET. That is a genuine limitation of the replay as an instrument, now measured rather than suspected.
- **THE LADDER STILL HAS NO INTERIOR OPTIMUM, so this is not a licence to widen.** Deepest excursions across the five: -3.67, -3.81, -5.12, -5.85, -6.01. A stop beyond ~-6.5% never fires at all, so "wider is better" continues to the degenerate limit exactly as `(fo)` found. And **two trades carry the entire +11.41pp** — n=5, with the sign flipping on WLD and DATA alone.
- **THE 4x CAPTURE GAP IS SUBSTANTIALLY SELECTION, NOT STRUCTURE.** The two arms drew different symbols from the same stream (live: SKHY x2, DRAM x2, 1000PEPE, ...; shadow: USELESS x2, DATA x3, MON, CXMT, ...) with **zero** shared `(pair, open-minute)` rows. The shadow simply drew names that did not hit their stops. So "close the capture gap" is NOT a standing opportunity — the live arm is not leaving money on the table, it drew worse in a 10-trade sample.
- **WHAT SHIPS: THE EXPERIMENT, NOT THE STOP.** The live arm stays at `-0.03`. `(fp)` pinned the tuner so a stop can never become an autonomous lever — correct, and unchanged — but it also removed the accidental A/B that was running. So the stop becomes a **declared shadow experiment**: `TT_SL=-0.04` set deliberately on the **$1k shadow twin only**, visible in `extra.bars`, while live holds `-0.03`. That restores the comparison as something OBSERVED rather than something an organ wandered into, and it is the paired live-vs-shadow structure `(fo)` itself prescribed. **Zero real money.**
- **`taker-live-bars.yml` gains `sync_tuner_sweep_sl`** (default yes): setting an arm's stop also sets `TUNER_SWEEP_SL` to match, so the tuner's still-active TP/HOLD sweep optimises against the bracket the arm is actually running rather than against `(fp)`'s pinned default. Input-validated `yes|no`; tested including the refusal path.
- **PRE-REGISTERED BAR for this experiment, written before it runs:** the shadow arm at `-0.04` must beat the live arm at `-0.03` on per-trade return over >=7 days AND >=30 shadow closes AND in both halves, before the live stop is reconsidered. Anything less and the answer stays `-0.03`. **n=5 is not evidence for a real-money change** — that is the whole lesson of `(fo)`, `(fm)` and `(fl)`.

## 2026-07-29 (fs) — CORRECTION: the live Taker does NOT have a negative edge. I graded ACROSS the bull-mode flip and pooled a retired policy with the live one

- **THE ERROR.** `(fp)` and `(fr)` both assert *"n=25, mean -0.183%/trade, t=-0.26 ... five of six go-live criteria fail, so there is no edge to tune into."* That number pools **two different policies**. `TT_BULL_MODE` went on **24-Jul** ((dh)) and switched the live arm from all-divergence to **short-divergence-crypto**.   | PRE-bull (retired policy) | 13 | **-0.780%** | 11 of 13 LONG-divergence |
  | POST-bull (current policy) | 12 | **+0.464%** | 11 of 12 SHORT-divergence |

  The losses belong to long-divergence — **the exact lens the bull gate exists to exclude.** The gate worked; the grading did not.
- **THE CURRENT POLICY'S REAL RECORD**, restricted to its own lens (short-divergence) in its own era, graded per ARM because these are two separate books (verified: **zero** shared `(pair, open-minute)` rows, so not double-counting):

  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | LIVE arm | 11 | +0.883% | +0.77 | +14.71 / **-5.00** pp |
  | SHADOW twin | 10 | **+3.484%** | **+5.13** | +19.51 / +15.33 pp |
  | pooled, de-duplicated | 21 | +2.122% | **+2.86** | both positive |

- **[CORRECTED, same day, by an independent regrade — "the edge is real" OVERSTATES it, in five specific ways.]**
  1. **ddof.** Every t above used POPULATION stdev. Sample stdev: live **+0.73** (not +0.77), shadow **+4.86** (not +5.13), pooled **+2.79** (not +2.86).
  2. **The "zero shared rows" separateness test was a FALSE NEGATIVE.** Minute-exact matching finds nothing because the arms open the same ticket 1-2 minutes apart.   **WHAT SURVIVES:** the era-pooling error was real and this correction's DIRECTION is right — the book is not demonstrably edge-dead, and a fleet-wide test clears the obvious confound (every other short book DEGRADED in the same window, +0.509% -> -0.043% on n=268->233, so this is not a short-friendly week). **The honest verdict is "promising, unproven, keep measuring", not "the edge is real".**

## 2026-07-29 (fq) — THE DASHBOARD'S HEADLINE AND THE STRATEGY'S EDGE CAN DISAGREE IN SIGN, and the go-live gate reads BOTH bases at once

- **THE MEASUREMENT.** `lighter-ticket-taker-lshadow`, n=135 closes: `/pnl.json` reports **+$6.93** — and the equal-weighted per-trade series sums to **-12.52pp** (mean **-0.093%/trade, t=-0.39**). Same book, same trades, **opposite signs**. The live arm's two bases happen to agree (-$0.18 / -0.183%/trade), which is exactly why the disagreement went unnoticed on the twin.
- **THE MECHANISM — sizing, not edge.** Implied stakes on this book run $20-$80 (median $26). The 51 winners average a **$48.3** stake; the 84 losers average **$36.1**. Winners are sized **1.34x** the losers, so a book that loses on the average trade still books a positive dollar total. That is the constant-risk sizer doing its job (smaller clips where the stop is further away), so the dollar figure is not *wrong* — but it is a statement about SIZING, and it is being read as a statement about EDGE.
- **THE GATE READS BOTH BASES AT ONCE** (`scripts/golive_readiness.py` `stats()`, measured not inferred): `mean` and `t` come from `pct` (equal-weighted, `r[0]`); `h1`, `h2`, `max_dd_usd` come from `pnl_abs` (dollar, `r[1]`). So one book can **PASS "both halves positive" on dollars while FAILING "mean > 0" on percentages** — and the shadow taker does exactly that right now (halves +$4.57 / +$2.36, mean -0.093%). "Both halves positive" therefore does not mean what a reader assumes it means; on this book it is carried by the sizer.
- **NOT CHANGED, DELIBERATELY.** The go-live bar is the operator's rule and was re-specified by him on 29-Jul; picking a single basis is his call, not a session's. Both bases are defensible (dollars are what the book earns; percentages are what the strategy earns) and the mix may even be intentional. This entry makes the behaviour EXPLICIT so the 4-Aug review can decide with the ambiguity in front of it, rather than discovering it inside a promotion.
- **CORRECTS (fm).** That entry cited *"shadow +$7.33 / 135 closes against live -$0.42 / 25 closes"* as the OUT-OF-SAMPLE corroboration for moving the live arm's bracket to the twin's bars. On the equal-weighted basis the twin is **negative** (-0.093%/trade, t=-0.39), so that corroboration does not hold and the argument was weaker than stated. `(fo)` had already reverted the change on independent grounds (the no-interior-optimum artifact); this removes its remaining support rather than changing any outcome.
- **THE GENERAL RULE, worth more than this instance.** A dollar total answers "what did the book earn"; a per-trade mean answers "does the strategy have an edge". When stakes vary they are different questions and can have different answers. **Quote the basis with the number, always** — and when citing a book as evidence FOR a strategy change, cite the equal-weighted series, because that is the one the change is about.
- Publish-only: no code, no lever, no book, no real money. The `/pnl.json` figure is unchanged and remains correct for what it measures.

At **10:46 UTC** `/bus.json` showed `fleet-tuning` carrying `taker.sl = -0.04`, `set_by: scout-tuner`, `expires 12:46:15Z` — **re-enacted every cycle**. The growth rail was autonomously walking back to the exact value the operator's own doctrine had just ruled void, and it would have kept doing so indefinitely on a 2h TTL.
- **VERIFIED IN THE SHADOW ARM'S OWN DEPLOYED FRAME** (bull on, tp .06, hold 72h, max_open 6, $50 clips, 200h/2397-snapshot Lighter tape) — not inherited from `(fo)`'s live-path measurement, re-run here because a different frame is a different surface:

  | stop | net $ | closed | wr % | # sl exits |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | -0.02 | -19.34 | 41 | 22.0 | 21 |
  | -0.03 | -15.10 | 31 | 29.0 | 12 |
  | **-0.04 (what the tuner enacted)** | **+9.81** | 22 | 45.5 | 4 |
  | -0.06 | +22.26 | 22 | 59.1 | 1 |
  | -0.12 | +30.05 | 21 | 61.9 | **0** |
  | **NO STOP** | **+30.05** | 21 | 61.9 | **0** |

  Monotone to the degenerate limit, no interior optimum, and the ladder simply stops changing once no stop ever fires. `SWEEP_SL` was running inside this surface every cycle and, by construction, choosing the widest value in its grid.
- **THE FIX — remove the actuator's authority over a knob its own instrument cannot measure.** Two independent protections, each separately asserted so removing EITHER turns the suite red:

  2. `STOP_LOSS` has **no entry in `attr_to_lever`**, so a stop cannot become a `fleet-tuning` lever even if the grid is widened again later. The levers comprehension now skips an unmapped attr (`if a in attr_to_lever`) rather than raising, since the sweep's candidate dict always carries all three keys.
- **RESTRICT-ONLY, SHADOW-ONLY, ZERO REAL MONEY.** `taker.*` levers live on the `lighter-taker` lane, which is the **$1k shadow** book; only `live.*` levers steer the live arm, and this touches none of them. It removes a capability, never adds one.
- **EXPECT THE SHADOW ROW'S HEADLINE NUMBER TO FALL** — on this tape from +$29.90 at `-0.04` to about +$14.77 at `-0.03`. That drop is the artifact being removed, not edge being lost, and it should not be read as a regression. Second-order benefit: the shadow arm stops being a moving target, which is a precondition for it ever serving as the experiment judge's control arm.
- **WHY THIS IS THE ONLY CHANGE SHIPPED FROM AN 11-AGENT OPTIMISATION CAMPAIGN.** The campaign's own verdict is that the taker is **capital-bound, not edge-bound**: the live arm holds $66.45 behind a $40 notional cap at ~$10 a clip, so even its measured per-trade rate is worth roughly **eleven cents a day**. Era-split, the CURRENT policy is POSITIVE — live short-divergence n=11 +0.883%/trade, shadow twin n=10 +3.484% t=+5.13, pooled t=+2.86 both halves. The edge is real; the book is capital-bound, not edge-dead. Nothing (fp) refutes is affected — the stop artifact is dead for unrelated reasons.]** Every widening candidate was refuted. The one defensible action was to stop an autonomous organ from re-arming a known artifact.
- **Tests**: 3 new assertions, each mutation-verified (re-widening `SWEEP_SL`, restoring the `STOP_LOSS` mapping, and making the comprehension raise instead of skip all turn the tuner selftest red). Suite green; born-dark 20, venue-purity 89.

## 2026-07-29 (fo) — THE EXIT-BRACKET CHANGE IS REVERTED: its evidence was the (fj) artifact, caught by an adversarial test I should have run BEFORE shipping

- **WHAT HAPPENED.** (fm) shipped `TT_TP 0.06 / TT_SL -0.04 / TT_MAX_HOLD_H 72` to the real-money Ticket Taker on a window-sensitivity table that looked strong (the twin's bars beat the deployed bars at every window, both halves positive at every window). - **THE TEST THAT KILLS IT — extend the ladder to NO STOP AT ALL** (live path, tp .06, hold 72h, $10 clips, 200h tape). Re-measured myself, not taken on the agent's word:

  | stop | net $ | n | wr % | # sl | worst trade | worst MAE |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | -0.02 | +1.14 | 42 | 31.0 | 29 | -4.01% | -3.93% |
  | -0.03 (deployed) | +4.14 | 34 | 47.1 | 18 | **-5.08%** | -5.00% |
  | -0.04 (shipped by (fm)) | +7.83 | 21 | 76.2 | 4 | **-7.42%** | -7.34% |

  | **NO STOP** | **+9.51** | 16 | 93.8 | **0** | **-3.35%** | -8.46% |

- **THE SIGNATURE, and it is one this repo already named TODAY.** Net climbs to the no-stop limit with no interior optimum — the textbook *"a wider stop stops realising losses that later revert"* artifact that **(fj)** identified and withdrew this same morning on the incubator's STOP_LOSS signal. I read the -0.04/-0.05 pair as a PLATEAU and declined the argmax on that basis. It was not a plateau; it was noise on a monotone climb, and declining the argmax gave the reasoning a rigour it did not have.
- **THE DECISIVE DETAIL: there is no tail in this window for a stop to cut.** With NO stop the worst realised trade is **-3.35%** — SMALLER than the deployed -3% stop's own worst trade (-5.08%) and less than HALF the -0.04 candidate's (-7.42%). On this tape the stop does not protect against the tail, it MANUFACTURES the realised loss: every adverse excursion reverted inside the hold. So the instrument cannot price a stop at all, and **every** `TT_SL` verdict drawn from it is void — the grid's, the agent's, and (fm)'s alike.
- **WHY REVERT RATHER THAN KEEP AND WATCH.** Widening a real-money stop is risk-INCREASING and it now has no supporting evidence. The honest asymmetry: a wider stop looks better on a tail-free window BY CONSTRUCTION, and this window is measurably tail-free. Reverting restores the operator's own configuration, which is the correct default when the case for changing it collapses. TP and HOLD went back with it — their sweeps were noisy (no clean shape at any stop setting) and were run at stop settings whose effect dominates them, so nothing in that bracket was independently supported.

That is a reason to DOUBT the deployed stop — not a validated replacement for it. The right instrument is the experiment judge's paired live-vs-shadow bar, not an env dispatch off a replay that cannot price the knob. Queued as a review item, not shipped.
- **PROCESS — the actual lesson, and it is the same one twice in one day.** (fm) was itself a retraction of (fl) for asserting a change without checking the receipt. (fo) is a retraction of (fm) for asserting a change without running the adversarial test that the repo's own doctrine already prescribes and that (fj) had demonstrated hours earlier on the very same knob. Both were caught, and both were caught by measurement rather than by review — but in each case the check existed and was run one step too late. **The sweep is not the evidence; the sweep plus the test that would falsify it is the evidence.**

## 2026-07-29 (fn) — THE TAKER IS NOT UNDER-TUNED, IT IS SWITCHED OFF: the live arm has been unable to take ANY entry for 33h, vetoed on a population it does not trade

- **THE FINDING.** The live real-money Ticket Taker's effective allowed-lens set is **EMPTY**, and has been since 2026-07-28T02:40Z (~33h, 28 consecutive brain runs). `allowed_lenses("lighter_live")` is `{divergence}` (hard allow-list) and the brain's lens veto — which is SENIOR and applied on top — currently vetoes `divergence`. Empty set means the entry loop skips every ticket. `/pnl.json` corroborates: `open_trades: 0`, last live entry 28-Jul 00:43Z. **No amount of tuning matters while the gate is shut**; this is why the taker is not "taking off".
- **THE MECHANISM — the veto grades the wrong population.** `bot_learn.grade_scout_lenses` sign-flips shorts (so it is direction-aware in SIGN) but aggregates per LENS, not per (lens, SIDE) — and `divergence` emits both directions. Meanwhile `TT_BULL_MODE` (on since 24-Jul) restricts BOTH taker arms to `(divergence, short)` + `(breakout/breakoutup, long)`. So the arm is judged on a book that is **69% long** while it trades **only short**. Re-derived on the 200h tape with the brain's OWN `episode_firsts` and sign convention:

  | population | eps4h | ehit4h | eavg4h % | verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | divergence POOLED (what is published + vetoed on) | 1006 | 0.483 | -0.093 | **VETO** |
  | divergence / **long** (69% of episodes) | 692 | 0.470 | -0.199 | veto — correctly |
  | divergence / **short** (what the arms trade) | 314 | **0.513** | **+0.139** | would NOT veto |
  | divergence / short / **crypto** (what the LIVE arm trades) | 158 | **0.525** | **+0.289** | would NOT veto |

  The losing long majority drags the pooled grade under the hard 0.500 bar and takes the winning short side with it. The lens the live arm is restricted to is the one the pool is killing.
- **THE FIX — grade the sub-population the arm actually trades.** `grade_scout_lenses` now ALSO publishes a nested `by_side` block per lens (same field names as the lens level, episode fields only, so a consumer can hand either dict to the same reader). Every existing field keeps its exact meaning — **no current consumer changes behaviour**. `lighter_ticket_taker.vetoed_lenses` gains an optional `sides` map (lens -> the ONE side this arm may take, derived from `BULL_LENS_SIDES` by the new `restricted_sides()`); when a `by_side` grade exists for that side AND meets the same floor, the verdict comes from it.
- **NOT A LOOSENING — it cuts both ways, and the test proves it.** An arm restricted to a side that grades BADLY inside a HEALTHY pool now gets vetoed where it previously was not. That assertion is in the selftest specifically so this cannot decay into a one-directional widening.
- **FAIL-SAFE to the pre-(fn) rule in every degraded case**: no `sides` (the tuner and the incubator pass none — both unchanged), no `by_side` block (a brain that has not redeployed yet), an unmet sub-floor, or the kill switch `TT_LENS_VETO_SIDE_AWARE=off` all fall back to the pooled grade byte-for-byte. Deploy order therefore does not matter: whichever of brain/taker lands first, the other side degrades to today's behaviour until both are up.
- **MEASURED END-TO-END against the live bus payload**: before, `vetoed = [breakout, divergence, momentum]` and the live allowed set is EMPTY; after, `vetoed = [breakout, momentum]` and the live allowed set is `[divergence]`. **The SHADOW arm gains `divergence` too** — stated plainly rather than buried, because it is a widening of a $1k book: bull mode restricts the shadow arm to short-divergence as well, so the same correction applies to it by the same argument (and short-divergence is that book's best lens, +$15.64 of a +$5.11 book).
- **THE HONEST LIMIT.** The un-veto rests on a POINT estimate. `divergence/short` Wilson lower bound is 0.477 and `short/crypto` is 0.474 — both still under the 0.500 bar. The veto rule reads the point estimate (that is its existing design, unchanged here), so the sub-population clears it, but this is "the pooled grade was measuring the wrong thing", not "the short side is proven good". n=314 / 158 episodes on ONE 200h tape in ONE falling regime.
- **Tests**: 5 new taker assertions + 7 brain checks, each mutation-verified (killing the side-aware branch, dropping the sub-floor check, ignoring BULL_MODE in `restricted_sides`, dropping the `by_side` emission, and mis-keying the side bucket all turn the suites RED). Suite 304 green; born-dark 20, venue-purity 89.
- **Credit**: surfaced by a multi-agent taker-optimisation workflow; every load-bearing number here was re-derived independently against the shipped code before anything was changed.

## 2026-07-29 (fm) — RETRACTION: the bull-mode "ship" was a no-op (it was already on since 24-Jul) — and the change that IS real, the live arm's exit bracket

- **THE ERROR, stated plainly.** (fl) reported shipping `TT_BULL_MODE=on` to the real-money Ticket Taker. It was already on. The operator set it himself on **24-Jul** and it is recorded two screens down in this same file ((dh): *"the operator flipped the LIVE taker to short-divergence-crypto (`TT_BULL_MODE=on` on `tide-rider-lighter-live`, verified `extra.bull=true`)"*). Reading `/pnl.json` after the dispatch showed `bull: true` on **both** arms — including the shadow arm nobody had just touched. That is only explicable if the flag predated the change.   |---|---|---|---|

On a ~$66 book with the $40 notional cap, the SafetyRails daily-loss halt and the kill switch all untouched, that is still contained, but it is ~45% deeper per trade and it is the number to hold in mind.

Those 4 go **3 tp / 1 sl**, +11.88 %pts against -14.01 %pts realised at `-0.03` — a real swing on **n=4**. The mechanism is coherent (a reversion short stopped at -3% is being knocked out of trades that revert: LIT -3.52% MAE -> +6.25%, BOT -3.69% -> +7.11%, DATA -3.58% -> +5.94%) and the one failure is the -7.42% above. - **Caveats kept in front.** n=10-21 closes per window is thin; it is ONE tape in ONE falling regime; the twin's bars were tuner-derived on overlapping tape, so the in-sample discount applies (the plateau shape and the twin's own out-of-sample ledger are what carry it, not the argmax). ## 2026-07-29 (fa) — the incubator stops hoarding duplicates and corpses; and the honest answer on "fresh options": there are none in-cage

Operator: *"learning from the incubator so it doesn't make or duplicate bots that don't achieve anything, dead genotypes disposed of and fresh new models and options to test."* Three asks; the first two were real defects and are fixed, the third is answered with measurements rather than invention.

- **The breeding side was already clean** — worth stating so nobody re-fixes it: `select_elite` demands `both_halves_pos`, so a losing genotype can never become a gamete. Every defect found was in the REGISTER.
- **`prune_register()` (new, pure, selftested) — dedupe / dispose / re-rank.** Measured on the live register: **64 entries → 32 kept, 32 duplicates collapsed**, and the register was sitting **AT the 64 cap**, so the defects below were actively evicting live genotypes.
  - **DUPLICATES.** Two genotypes differing only in genes the current veto makes unevolvable are ONE experiment — the organ cannot tell them apart, and showing both invents a roster. Collapsed on the genotype REDUCED to currently-evolvable genes; the freshest representative survives and carries `merged_dupes`.
  - **IMMORTAL CORPSES — the worst of the three.** Cap eviction sorted dormants by `best_lcb`, a HIGH-WATER MARK, so one lucky historical score outranked every recently-measured genotype forever. Ranking is now on the LATEST reading, with entries scored this cycle ahead of any dormant.
  - **DISPOSAL, and it names which kind of dead**: `INERT` (dormant, never traded — achieves nothing) vs `LOSING` (dormant, fired and lost). Denominated in cycles seen and the latest reading, **never** `best_net` — the whole failure being fixed is a lucky score outliving the measurement that refuted it. Fail-safe throughout: never retires on unknown staleness, on a genotype scored this cycle, below the cycle floor, or on a positive latest reading; and the whole pass is skipped on a short tape (no scoring, no disposal). Disposal is REPORTED on `register_hygiene`, never silent.
- **"Fresh new models and options" — measured, and there are none available inside the cages.** Stated plainly because manufacturing some is exactly the behaviour being asked to stop:
  - **Every one of the 7 taker gene grids already spans its registry bounds exactly** (brk_range 0.90–0.97, dip_range 0.05–0.15, momo_chg 3–6, div_gap_pp 37.5–87.5, tp 0.03–0.06, sl −0.04…−0.02, max_hold 24–72). Zero unused headroom — new alleles would need a cage widening, which is an evidence/operator decision (the A1 class).
  - **One unbred registry lever existed** — `taker.sl_cooldown_h`, the same shape as the DIV_GAP_PP gap closed on 17-Jul, and the replay mirrors it faithfully so it IS measurable. Swept before proposing it: it is live **versus OFF** (0h → −$15.80 vs −$7.00) but **inert across its usable range** — 1h through 24h spans **$1.88**, against a one-fill swing of $3.50. Breeding it would mint genotypes differing by less than the evidence quantum ([[incubator-evidence-denominated-in-fills]]). **REJECTED on measurement**, recorded so nobody re-proposes it.
  - Finer resolution inside the existing spans was also rejected: the whole taker surface is negative on this window (default genome −$24.73 all-lens), so a finer search only searches a losing surface more finely.
- 5 mutations each turn their named assertion red: disposal reading `best_net`, retiring on unknown staleness, retiring a genotype scored this cycle, ranking on the high-water mark, and deduping on the full genotype. Suite 303; four guards green. Publish-only — no lever, no book, no row.
